latin: Quia intellectus animalis differt ab intellectu intellectuali ut pars media, non ut pars tantum, ideo intellectuali totalitati magis parificatur.
translation: Because the animal intellect differs from the intellectual intellect as a middle part, and not merely as a part, it is therefore the more made equal to the intellectual totality.
translation_note: 'Pars media' (a mediating, not merely a subordinate, part) continues the part/whole vocabulary of the immediately preceding thesis, 3>64 (farmer1998:21270).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch14, from Latin at farmer1998:21274
attribution: Among the conclusions Pico titles 'paradoxical, according to his own opinion, introducing new teachings in philosophy' (kabbalah_paradigma:1322).
doctrine: The thesis refines the preceding one's part/whole account of intellect by distinguishing a merely subordinate part from a 'middle' or mediating part, holding that the animal intellect, because it mediates, is thereby more nearly equalized to the intellectual totality than a plain part would be (farmer1998:21274).
historiography: The one study that cites this thesis in the material consulted quotes it immediately after 3>64 and before 3>66 in a single footnote, treating the three as a connected sequence (kabbalah_paradigma:1322).
not_established: No discussion of this thesis's doctrinal content, beyond its citation alongside 3>64 and 3>66, is found in the sources consulted.
